gridAndLayout.description: Our grid is built on an 8px base unit. All spacing, sizing, and breakpoints derive from multiples of 8.
rules: Gutters are always 8px or 16px (1x or 2x base unit). Never arbitrary values.
Page margin scales by breakpoint — 24px → 32px → 40px. Content never touches the edge.
Max content width is 1400px, centered. Beyond that, margins grow.
All component padding, gaps, and margins must be a multiple of the 8px base unit. Half-step (4px) allowed for icon alignment only.
Use border-box sizing. Borders draw inward — never let a 1px border break your 8px rhythm.

sectionReveal.description: IntersectionObserver-based scroll reveal. Elements start at opacity:0 and translateY(30px), transitioning to visible when entering viewport. Observer disconnects after reveal.

css.transition: opacity var(--duration-slower) var(--ease-spring), transform var(--duration-slower) var(--ease-spring)

implementation.methodology: Vanilla CSS with :root custom properties and semantic class names. No utility classes in HTML markup.
implementation.sectionPadding: Always use longhand padding-top/padding-bottom for vertical spacing. Never use shorthand padding on sections that also carry .page-container.
implementation.semanticClassNames: Use descriptive names like .section-heading, .timeline-card, .feature-card — not utility strings.

layoutComposition.description: Three layout strategies chosen based on content needs

responsive.description: Fluid columns — content scales with viewport. Column count stays fixed, width stretches.

adaptive.description: Fixed boxes that wrap — items have fixed size and tile across. Count grows with width.
adaptive.useFor: Card grids, icon toolbars, product listings

strict.description: No flex, scroll instead — fixed dimensions that don't scale. Horizontal scroll below threshold.
strict.useFor: Data tables, code blocks, complex forms

layoutComposition.decisionTree:
Does the user need to see more items or more content per item?
→ More items → Adaptive (fixed boxes that wrap)
→ More content → Responsive (fluid columns)
Would shrinking below a certain size harm legibility?
→ Yes → Strict (scroll at breakpoint)
→ No → Responsive

usageGuidelines: Use vanilla CSS with custom properties in :root
Semantic class names only (no utility strings)
Longhand padding for sections (never shorthand with .page-container)

designPrinciples.name: Balance
designPrinciples.usage: Align elements on an invisible axis; pair heavy text blocks with ample white space

designPrinciples.name: Contrast
designPrinciples.usage: Pair light and dark, large and small, bold and thin to guide the eye

designPrinciples.name: Emphasis
designPrinciples.usage: Use size, color, or position to make CTAs and key info unmissable — only one hero per screen

designPrinciples.name: Movement
designPrinciples.usage: Use spacing, arrows, and progressive disclosure to lead users through content

designPrinciples.name: Pattern
designPrinciples.usage: Repeat button styles, card layouts, and spacing rhythms across pages

designPrinciples.name: Proportion
designPrinciples.usage: Headings larger than body; icons proportional to text; containers sized to content

designPrinciples.name: Repetition
designPrinciples.usage: Reuse token values everywhere; never introduce new styles without updating the system

designPrinciples.name: Rhythm
designPrinciples.usage: Apply the 8px grid strictly; equal gaps between cards; consistent section padding

designPrinciples.name: Unity
designPrinciples.usage: Use shared tokens, consistent borders, and matching radii

designPrinciples.name: Hierarchy
designPrinciples.usage: Use size, weight, color, and position for clear reading order

designPrinciples.name: Variety
designPrinciples.usage: Alternate card orientations, mix image and text blocks, vary component density

designPrinciples.name: White Space
designPrinciples.usage: Use spacing tokens to create visual breathing room — margins are not wasted space
